title: Atomic Resolution Imaging of 2D Polymers with Tilt-corrected Bright Field (tcBF) Imaging
content: The field of polymer science has rapidly evolved, expanding from traditional linear chains and cross-linked networks to the emerging class of two-dimensional (2D) polymers [1]. These materials exhibit unique structural and functional properties distinct from covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and other porous polymeric materials. However, a major challenge in this field is the precise determination of 2D polymer structures, which is crucial for understanding their structure-property relationships and guiding rational synthesis. Traditional techniques like powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) often struggle to resolve the atomic structure due to the difficulty of growing large single crystals and the presence of mild disorder. This limitation hinders the accurate characterization of 2D polymers and their further development.
